book: The Book of the Dead — Selections

1: [Book of the Dead, ch. 1 — The going forth by day]

Here begin the chapters of going forth by day, of ascending into the light, of knowing the souls of the horizon. O you who are in the hall of the two truths, I have come to you, that I may be purified and may behold the Lord of All, and may go forth by day in every form I desire.
[Book of the Dead, ch. 1 — The heart's memory]

My heart of my mother, my heart of my mother — stand not up against me as a witness, oppose me not at the tribunal, make not thy voice against me before the keeper of the scales. I have done no wrong upon the earth; I have given bread to the hungry and water to the thirsty, and my heart remembers, and my heart will not accuse me.
2: [Book of the Dead, ch. 30B — The weighing of the heart]

They place the heart in the balance against the feather of Ma'at, which is truth. And Thoth, the scribe of the gods, records the weighing. If the heart is heavy with deeds undone, the devourer waits; if it is light with truth, the way opens, and the gates of the horizon are lifted, and the name is spoken, and the name is enough.
[Book of the Dead, ch. 30B — The declarations]

I have not done iniquity; I have not robbed; I have not slain men; I have not made the measure small; I have not taken the milk from the mouths of children; I have not driven cattle from their pastures; I have not fished in the marshes of the river-god; I have not extinguished a fire in its season; I have not obstructed the flow of running water; I am pure, I am pure, I am pure, I am pure.
3: [Book of the Dead, ch. 125 — The hall of two truths]

O ye gods who are in the hall of the two truths, I have come to you without sin, without guilt, without evil. I have not done that which the gods abominate; I have given bread to the hungry, water to the thirsty, clothing to the naked, and a boat to him who was stranded. I have made offerings to the gods and oblations to the dead. Deliver me, protect me — I am one of you.
[Book of the Dead, ch. 148 — The seven cows]

The seven cows and the bull provide the milk of life for the justified soul. Their names are the names of the days, and their milk is the river of the days, and he who knows their names shall not want, and he who pours out for others shall have his own vessel filled.
[Book of the Dead, ch. 175 — The breath of life]

O my father Osiris, I have come to you that I may be among your followers, for you are the king of those who are in the west. Grant that my soul may not perish, grant that my name may not be forgotten, grant me the breath of life as you grant it to the stars — for the stars are the souls of the justified, and they sail in your barque forever.
